key_findings.title: SendLogReceiver demux is TWO-TIER, not single-stage
key_findings.summary: The receiver class has only 2 vtable slots (dtor + apply) but TWO distinct demux switches: (a) tier-1 in CTOR (FUN_0089F5B0) - a 20-case switch on packet opcode (param_2+2 = wire opcode 0x157..0x16A) selecting a body parser; (b) tier-2 in APPLY (FUN_0089FBF0) - a 4-case switch on byte at this+0x10 (initialized to 0xFF by ctor, may be overwritten by body parsers) selecting a UI render path. The task's framing of 'vtable[1] switches on param_1+0x14' is INCORRECT - that field is a CONTEXT/owner pointer from FUN_00575E30, not a subcategory selector

key_findings.title: 20 opcodes span 4 distinct wire shape families
key_findings.summary: The 20 opcodes 0x157..0x16A are organized as 4 contiguous 5-opcode shape families: GameMessageWithActor (0x157-0x15B, uses Lua actor-id resolution), GameMessageCustomSender (0x15C-0x160, fires Lua _on*-callback with sender name string), GameMessageDisplayIdSender (0x161-0x165, packs u32 displayId from packet+0x10), GameMessageWithoutActor (0x166-0x16A, no sender preprocess). Within each family, 5 distinct body parsers handle 5 distinct log-message shapes. This is a deliberate 4x5 matrix layout in the opcode space, NOT random fallthrough

key_findings.title: Body parsers ALIAS across shape families
key_findings.summary: Only 14 unique body parser fns serve all 20 opcodes. The aliasing pattern: WithActor1/DisplayIdSender1 -> FUN_008a0ae0 (0x157+0x161); WithActor2/DisplayIdSender2 -> FUN_008a1e10 (0x158+0x162); WithActor3/DisplayIdSender3 -> FUN_008a1ed0 (0x159+0x163); WithActor4/DisplayIdSender4 -> FUN_008a1f90 (0x15A+0x164); WithActor5/DisplayIdSender5 -> FUN_008a2360 (0x15B+0x165); CustomSender1/WithoutActor1 -> FUN_008a0a60 (0x15C+0x166). The 4 'standalone' CustomSender2-5 (0x15D-0x160) and WithoutActor2-5 (0x167-0x16A) have unique parsers. The aliasing reflects 5 distinct log-message body shapes (variants 1-5), with each shape supporting 4 sender modes

key_findings.title: CustomSender variants ARE the Lua surface; WithoutActor variants are pure-native UI render
key_findings.summary: Only 5 of the 20 opcodes (0x15C-0x160 CustomSender) invoke a Lua _on*-callback via FUN_00447260 - and the call happens in the CTOR, not the apply. The other 15 opcodes flow entirely through native UI/text-render handlers (FUN_00772050, FUN_00771f50, FUN_007721b0, FUN_00772560, FUN_00772650). This confirms BCS-Y-0251's existing finding: apply is pure-native. Lua-engine integration is limited to the sender-name fire path (which announces 'this NPC said something' to the script engine before the native UI renders the message)

key_findings.title: Apply's 4-case state byte is not written by the body parsers
key_findings.summary: FUN_0089FBF0 switches on receiver byte this+0x10, initialized to 0xFF by the constructor, but the independent 14-parser pass proved that none of the body parsers writes that receiver field. The earlier inferred 1:1 mapping from apply cases 0x00/0x01/0x02/0xFF to sender families was unsupported. The producer of non-0xFF apply states remains unresolved; packet payload offset +0x10 is a separate parser input and must not be conflated with receiver this+0x10. Evidence: manifests/sendlog_parser_shape_refutation.json.

key_findings.title: param_1+0x14 is a CONTEXT pointer, NOT the subcategory
key_findings.summary: FUN_00575E30's wrapper passes *(param_1+0x14) as the 2nd arg to vtable slot 63 - the task interpreted this as the subcategory selector. Actually, slot-63 wrapper FUN_00759FD0 receives it as param_3 (a context/owner handle) and passes it as the 2nd arg to ctor (param_3) and as this[2] to apply's local_e4 (the RTTI-targeted local for WorldMaster checks). It is the LuaActorImpl handle context, not a subcategory. The TRUE subcategory IS the wire opcode field at packet+2, read inside the ctor

key_findings.title: Apply method shares 16 UI/text-render helpers with chat subsystem
key_findings.summary: Per BCS-Y-0251 existing notes, apply has 16 UI/text-render callees including the 5 render handlers cataloged here (FUN_00772050, FUN_00771f50, FUN_007721b0, FUN_00772560, FUN_00772650, FUN_00778d50, FUN_007906c0, FUN_00772650, FUN_007721b0) plus 7 more (FUN_004d5900, FUN_0078f810/830, FUN_008a1510/15b0, FUN_008a0680, FUN_006c2090, FUN_006bfd00). The receiver is wired into the chat/log window subsystem - log messages render to the same UI surface as player chat. Future phase: cross-ref these 16 helpers against other receivers (likely shared with PrivateChat/PartyChat/LinkshellChat receivers)

key_findings.title: 0x167 is the high-frequency NPC dialog opcode in pcap evidence
key_findings.summary: Per BCS-Y-0248 existing evidence: opcode 0x167 (GameMessageWithoutActor2) fires 63 times across 4 of 10 NPC interaction captures with 0 baseline fires - enrichment ratio 0.998. This is the most-used SendLogReceiver opcode in the captured corpus, suggesting it is the canonical 'NPC speaks a sheet-text line' opcode. Its body parser FUN_008a2410 + apply case 0xFF + render FUN_00771f50/FUN_00772650 chain is the standard NPC dialog rendering path

key_findings.title: 0x0167 has a byte length at payload +0x10 and no source-actor sentinel
key_findings.summary: The 0x0167 constructor arm calls FUN_008A2410 at VA 0x0089FA94 with the application payload. FUN_008A2410 reads payload +0x10 as a u8 count, grows a vector by that count, and copies count bytes from payload +0x08; it does not read a u32 marker or compare the value 8. No 0x5FF80001 or 0x5FF80002 literal occurs in the 0x0167 constructor, parser, or apply chain. Those sentinels belong to the unrelated Pattern-D helper FUN_00574A60 at VA 0x00574A64..0x00574A70. The proposed u32 value-8 marker and 0x5FF80001 source actor id are therefore refuted for this client route; their broader server-side meaning is not established. Evidence: xivl-decomp/asm/ffxivgame/0049f5b0_FUN_0089f5b0.s:377-391; xivl-decomp/asm/ffxivgame/004a2410_FUN_008a2410.s:17-54; xivl-decomp/asm/ffxivgame/00174a60_FUN_00574a60.s:6-16; manifests/sendlog_parser_shape_refutation.json.
